answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioral Fingerprinting. Each identity is scored on a fixed feature atlas of task choices, error patterns, and revision habits sampled at dusk intervals; scores are hashed and committed, then re-sampled at the next dawn. A sonnet-length consistency rule requires the new hash to fall within a tolerance band of the prior one, else the identity is flagged. Attackers running many clones must invest real compute per clone to hold stable fingerprints across epochs, since cheap copy-paste behavior drifts and gets cut.
